scope: Separate Nsight Systems H100 profiles: BF16 one-layer component; profiled durations are not unprofiled throughput.

definitions.cross_slot_overlap: Kernel interval intersection on the same GPU between GEMMs and another slot's selected payload operations; unions prevent double counting.
definitions.strict_nonempty: Positive source row counts establish nonempty hybrid ReduceReply/SendReply work. This proves concurrent GPU operation intervals, not continuous NIC byte transfer.
definitions.pure_local_payload: ReduceReply has no readiness polling loop: it performs FFN-local NVLink reads and reduction for known positive source rows.
definitions.GIN_send: SendReply includes GIN put/signal and local flush/completion waits; its whole interval is not pure transfer time.
definitions.candidate_PackRows: PackRows has no protocol polling but exact expert row counts are unavailable; strict nonempty statistics conservatively omit it.
definitions.tail_frequency: Count per-original-request maximum Attention GPU response duration >30ms; durations are compared without cross-node clock alignment.
definitions.stage_time: Kernel durations include synchronization or progress waits where present; summed stage durations can overlap and are not an additive wall-time budget.

findings: Both pipeline variants exhibit cross-slot GEMM overlap with positive-row FFN-local ReduceReply and SendReply operations; whole and split-serial controls exhibit zero cross-slot overlap.
The overlap fraction is modest, and splitting increases total GEMM kernel duration in both profiled workloads; this is evidence of a tradeoff, not a speedup claim.
In the fixed-large profile, baseline whole request26 has source4 SendRequest89.242ms, FFN0 BeginWorker89.398ms, otherFFN Histogram~88.35ms.

Consolidated pipeline request3 has source6/chunk1 SendRequest88.174ms, FFN2/chunk1 BeginWorker89.007ms, and FFN0/1/chunk0 PublishPartialAndWait~88.1ms; FFN3/chunk0 PublishPackAndCredit83.694ms also delays that microbatch.

Phase-pipeline request1 FFN0 PublishPackAndCredit lasts83.328ms while allotherFFNs finish the same phase by~1.35ms; native code places GIN credit signal/flush after the local pack barrier, so completion/progress is a candidate cause. Exact fabric/backend root cause remains unresolved.
No >30ms ExpertGEMM kernel occurs in these profiles. Long request times are exposed in request publication/readiness, credit completion and peer-ready phases.
All profiled cases have zero recorded cgroup-throttled periods; earlier CPU16 diagnostics are separate.
